Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring public agencies, special purpose districts, and municipalities to post certain information on their web sites.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to posting information on public agencies' websites; adding a new section to chapter 42.30 RCW; providing aneffective date; and declaring an emergency.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 42.30 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The agenda of all regular meetings of the governing body ofevery public agency, special purpose district, and any municipalitythat owns or maintains a web site shall be posted within seventy-twohours before a meeting. The agenda of all special or emergencymeetings shall be posted within twentyfour hours before a meeting.The posting shall indicate if the agendas are in draft form. (2) The text of any ordinance, rule, or regulation that is underconsideration at the meeting shall be included on the web site at thesame time the agenda is posted. (3) The minutes of all regular and special meetings of thegoverning body of every public agency, special purpose district, andany municipality that owns or maintains a web site shall be posted p. 1 SB 5553within fifteen business days after a meeting. The posting shallindicate if the minutes are in draft form or adopted. All postingsunder this section shall remain on the web site for one calendar year. (4) Every public agency, special purpose district, and anymunicipality that owns or maintains a public internet web site shall atall times have posted to it a roster of the names of all members of itsgoverning body, identifying the positions, and constituency whereapplicable, of all members. The web site shall at all times provideboth the start date and end date of the elective or appointed terms ofall members. (5) Subsections (1) through (3) of this section do not apply to thefollowing public agencies, municipalities, or their respectivesubagencies: (a) Counties with a population of less than twentythousand; (b) cities or towns with a population of less than eightthousand; or (c) school districts or special purpose districtsproviding services to a population of less than one thousand. (6) This section shall not be construed to affect existing publicagency notice requirements in RCW 42.30.060 or 42.30.075.
This act is necessary for the immediatepreservation of the public peace, health, or safety, or support of thestate government and its existing public institutions, and takes effectJuly 1, 2011.
